item.title: How 'Sopranos' star Vincent Pastore helped create the single greatest television season of all time
item.description: Vincent Pastore's Big Pussy drove the finest season of television ever made, from FBI informant reveals to fever dreams and a final boat ride.
item.content:encoded:
Fans of the "Sopranos" are still reeling from the loss of beloved star Vincent Pastore over the weekend.

The veteran actor known for playing Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero on the HBO crime drama was found dead in his Bronx home, and although he was only on the show for two seasons, his passing left a giant hole in the "Sopranos" community.

You can count me in as one of those fans who was particularly bummed to lose Pastore, because he contributed to what is perhaps the finest season of television that has ever been gifted to mankind.

RANKING THE MAJOR ANTAGONISTS OF 'THE SOPRANOS'

It's no secret that I love "The Sopranos," as a quick scroll through some of my work will yield a smattering of articles pontificating on every aspect of the show.

It's one of my favorite series of all time, and season two in particular represents what is, in my humble opinion, the apex of episodic television.

This is thanks in large part to Pastore's contributions as Tony Soprano's best friend and loyal soldier, Big Pussy.

Throughout most of season one, we are shown that Puss is Tony's confidant, even more so than his second-in-command, Silvio Dante.

Tony goes to Puss for advice about his son, among other things, showing the two have a connection that goes far beyond "the business."

But by the end of the first season, Puss is suspected to be an informant for the FBI, and before anyone from the Soprano crew can confirm their suspicions, he takes off for parts unknown, only setting off more alarm bells for Tony and company.

When he returns at the beginning of season two with an airtight alibi — going to Puerto Rico for acupuncture therapy to treat his ailing back — he has to re-earn the trust of his fellow crew members.

What makes Pussy's return unique, however, is that it is revealed early in the second season to the audience only that he's actually a rat, and the rest of the season is spent watching Tony subconsciously piecing together the evidence that his best friend is working with the feds to take him down.

It makes for riveting television the entire season, as we get several moments of tension as viewers know that Pussy has turned state's witness and could get whacked at any time.

Pussy's heel turn also gives us more insight into the FBI's inner workings, as the Bureau starts to become more of a main character thanks to the show focusing on his forced partnership with them.

This all culminates in the moment Tony finally figures it out, and the methods through which he arrives at the conclusion that his soldier is playing for the other team are some of the most creative and twisted in all of television.

In the penultimate episode of season two, Tony's biggest competition, Richie Aprile, gets taken out by his fiancée (Tony's sister Janice).

This happens right as Richie is about to make a move on Tony to take him out, so with one episode to wrap up the season, it appears as if all of Tony's worries are behind him.

Then we are reminded of the elephant — or in this case, rat — in the room.

After a late night meal at an Indian restaurant followed by a nightcap at the crew's favorite Italian restaurant, a season's worth of suspicions comes bubbling up for Tony in the form of a violent episode of food poisoning.

While deep in the throes of his intestinal Hell, Tony has a series of fever dreams that start out as subtle warnings and end up practically spelling it out for him.

"You know I've been working for the feds, right Ton'," a fish with Pussy's voice says to Tony.

It's so unique and brilliant, and I have no idea how the writers even came up with something like that, but it's easily my favorite hour of television ever made.

‘SOPRANOS’ STAR LORRAINE BRACCO SAYS SHE'S LOOKING FOR LOVE IN HER 70S

After that revelation, Tony and his crew take Pussy on a final, ill-fated boat ride where the compromised mobster cops to his crimes against the family before reminiscing on old times and sharing a final drink as Tony, Silvio, and Paulie draw their guns.

"You were like a brother to me. To all of us."

Before they have a chance to change their minds, the three heartbroken crew members unload their weapons into Pussy's chest and give him a burial at sea.

The episode and season end with a montage of all the destruction Tony and his crew have caused throughout the 13-episode run, interspersed with the mob boss enjoying the "fruits of his labor" at his daughter Meadow's high school graduation, blissfully unaware of (or unaffected by) the pain he's inflicted on his community.

The final shot lingers on the crashing waves of the North Jersey shoreline, reminding us of Pussy's ultimate fate, as the show fades to black while the haunting tones of The Rolling Stones' "Thru and Thru" play in the background.

It's perfect.

A perfect ending to a nearly perfect season of television.

And it's not just the Big Pussy storyline that makes season two must-watch TV, either.

The aforementioned Richie Aprile, played wonderfully by David Proval, makes for one of the most menacing villains of the series.

His back-and-forth with Tony throughout the season is equal parts hysterical and frightening, and he represents one of our protagonist's most formidable foes.

Season two also introduces another fan favorite to the cast in Furio Giunta, the native Italian who acts as Tony's enforcer and causes plenty of consternation between he and Pussy, as the latter (correctly) believes he is being replaced by the former.

And I would be remiss if I didn't mention Tony's mother, Livia, who proves to be a bigger thorn in his side than even Richie at times throughout the show's run.

Nancy Marchand's turn as the morose, sociopathic matriarch of the Soprano family deserves special mention, particularly because she turned in such a masterful performance while battling the very cancer that would ultimately cost the actress her life shortly after season two wrapped.

"The Sopranos" would experience more highs throughout its six-ish season run, but none ever reached the zenith that was season two, in my opinion.

The writers are firing on all cylinders, the cast of characters is robust, and the plot lines are engaging enough to leave you begging for more at the end of each episode.

And none of it would have had the cultural impact it did if not for everyone's favorite FBI rat.

item.title: Republican who reportedly dropped out defeats Trump's pick in key swing-district primary
item.description: Trump-endorsed Amir Hassan lost the Republican primary in Michigan's 8th District to Thomas J. Smith, who will now face Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet.
item.content:encoded:
Republican voters in Michigan's 8th Congressional District chose Thomas J. Smith as their challenger to freshman Democratic Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet on Wednesday – defying President Donald Trump's endorsement of opponent Amir Hassan – in one of several House races the GOP hopes will help expand its majority in November.

The district stretches across Flint, Saginaw, Midland and Bay City, and has become increasingly competitive in recent election cycles. Al Lemmo also vied for the nomination.

Smith was a longtime GM employee, according to his website.

"We need strong conservative leadership that protects our constitutional freedoms, supports working families, secures our borders, and restores accountability in Washington," he said on his website.

Smith reportedly suspended his campaign in July and endorsed Lemmo, according to the Detroit News, while Trump endorsed Hassan and invited him onstage at a recent rally.

Hassan spoke then about how many members of his family worked for GM. "The contrast is clear, the time is now," Hassan said. "Protecting America, getting back to the fundamentals… that’s what we’re doing this cycle."

HOUSE REPUBLICANS AIM TO TURN DEMOCRATIC CIVIL WAR INTO MIDTERM WEAPON

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Lemmo, a retired Army automotive mechanical engineer, ran on a pro-life and pro-onshoring platform.

DEMOCRATS TARGET MORE GOP HOUSE SEATS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES ROCK LEFT-WING PRIMARIES

Smith recorded just over 50% of the vote by Wednesday morning, and was declared the winner by the Associated Press.

Smith told the Detroit News he is "humbled and honored that Republicans have chosen me to take the fight to Kristen McDonald Rivet."

Rivet, who was a state senator representing Bay City before her tenure in Congress, won her primary Tuesday.

She defeated the GOP's Paul Junge by about six points in 2024's contests.

item.title: Brandt Snedeker is right to shut down the outside demand for younger Presidents Cup picks
item.description: Brandt Snedeker played a practice round with Jackson Koivun but says he won't pick young players for the Presidents Cup just for the sake of youth.
item.content:encoded:
There are bad problems, and there are good problems, and Brandt Snedeker has a whole bunch of the latter.

In less than 50 days, the 2026 Presidents Cup will get underway at Medinah Country Club, where the U.S. team will look to defeat the Internationals for the 11th straight time. Snedeker, the captain of the U.S. side, will have six of his 12 players selected for him via automatic qualifying, and then comes the inevitable difficult decisions surrounding his six captain's picks to round out his team.

With the Presidents Cup being both entirely lopsided and a gargantuan rung below the Ryder Cup on the ladder of significance, there is always pressure for a youth movement to be embraced by the U.S. team. Snedeker may be facing that pressure more than any other captain in the Cup's 30-year history, but he isn't succumbing to it, at least not yet.

Those pressures of bringing the 'kids' along to Medinah became as obvious as ever before over the past two weeks with 21-year-old Jackson Koivun winning the 3M Open in just his third start as a professional and 24-year-old Michael Thorbjornsen winning the Rocket Classic for his maiden PGA Tour victory.

Given Koivun's insanely impressive amateur and college career at Auburn and his nearly-immediate win on Tour, much of the golf world went ahead and wrote his name in Sharpie to be named to the Presidents Cup team. Thorbjornsen's name has been penciled in, although he's been sneakily fantastic in his short PGA Tour career.

Snedeker played a practice round with Koivun ahead of this week's Wyndham Championship, and while he praised his game and called him a "generational" player, he made it clear his strategy as captain does not involve bringing on youth for the sake of bringing on youth.

"I don't ever really look at it like we have to change things or do things different. I think the golf dictates who needs to be on the team. I'm not into, 'oh, let's just take a young kid because we need a young kid on the team,'" Snedeker said on Tuesday.

"That doesn't make any sense to me. I think you take the best players who give you the best opportunity of winning. I don't think -- you can't discount what people have done and you can't -- it's really hard to forecast how guys are going to handle those kinds of things. You look at how they've played, what they're capable of, what their ceiling is, what their basement is, what their floor is and kind of go from there."

Snedeker's comments represent the polar opposite viewpoints that leadership in place and golf fans have when looking at the Presidents Cup, but that doesn't mean what he had to say about the situation is wrong.

From a fan's perspective, and it's an understandable one, the Presidents Cup is a warm-up event for the Ryder Cup. With that mindset, why wouldn't Koivun be given a spot on the U.S. team and get match-play reps at the Presidents Cup, when it's assumed he will play his way onto the very short list of players who could represent the red, white, and blue at the 2027 Ryder Cup?

It's a fair question, especially when the U.S. Ryder Cup team has lost nine of the last 12 Ryder Cups dating back to the turn of the century, and needs to (must) try a new approach in 2027.

While Snedeker absolutely wants to see the U.S. team go to Ireland and upset Team Europe in 2027, that is not part of his job description as this year's Presidents Cup captain.

Snedeker's lone objective is putting together the best 12-player roster he can to avoid becoming just the second U.S. captain to ever lose the Presidents Cup. That could, and more likely than not will, include taking Koivun and other young, up-and-coming players to Medinah, but it shouldn't be an absolute certainty simply because there is a Ryder Cup to be played 12 months down the road and those players may be in the mix to make that team.

I'll join the masses and go on record in saying Koivun should be on the U.S. Presidents Cup team, but I also understand that Snedeker is not in the future-telling business; he's in the business of winning the Presidents Cup, and anything that may come after that shouldn't take over the decision-making process for the first-time captain.

item.title: Republicans move to oust embattled Florida GOP lawmaker in bitter primary fight
item.description: Reps. Cory Mills, Chuck Edwards and Max Miller face misconduct allegations that now threaten GOP control of Congress heading into midterms. Edwards has dropped his campaign.
item.content:encoded:
House GOP divisions are erupting on the midterm campaign trail as Republicans fight an uphill battle to keep control of Congress for the latter half of President Donald Trump's term.

The infighting touched down in Florida on Wednesday, where two House Republicans are endorsing a primary opponent to incumbent Rep. Cory Mills, R-Fla., who is facing multiple investigations into his finances and allegations of domestic abuse, among other claims. Mills has denied any wrongdoing.

Reps. Mike Haridopolos, R-Fla., and Anna Paulina Luna, R-Fla., announced they're backing former sports reporter Ryan Elijah for Mills' seat and said they "urge our fellow Republicans to join us in supporting him."

"Ryan Elijah is an excellent candidate and will ensure victory for us in Florida 7," Haridopolos told Fox News Digital.

GOP PARTY FISSURES EXPOSED IN BATTLE FOR S.C. SENATE SEAT TO REPLACE GRAHAM: 'I DON'T LIKE HEARING THAT'

Notably, President Donald Trump has endorsed Haridopolos, Luna and Mills for re-election.

It comes after another GOP source told Fox News Digital that some Florida Republicans were worried about the chances of keeping Mills' seat if he won the primary on Tuesday, Aug. 18.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report downgraded its projection for Republicans from "Solid R" to "Likely R" earlier this year. And with a Cook rating of R+5, Democrats could be within striking distance if Republicans see a tough enough cycle in November.

Mills is under investigation by the House Ethics Committee and the Department of Justice (DOJ), according to a source, though he has consistently insisted that he has not done anything wrong.

WATCH: CORY MILLS BLASTS DOJ PROBE AS ‘POLITICAL OP' AHEAD OF FLORIDA PRIMARY

The Republican military veteran dismissed reports of a DOJ investigation as a "desperate lie" by his opponents and said on X late last month, "We are not aware of any DOJ investigation, nor has there been any confirmation of such investigation by DOJ or FBI, and would fully cooperate if there was one."

Fox News Digital reached out to Mills for a response to Haridopolos and Luna's endorsement.

Mills is one of several House Republicans whose allegations of misconduct are posing a headache for the GOP on the campaign trail.

Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announced overnight that he would drop his re-election bid after an explosive report detailed sexual harassment accusations by two young female staffers. Edwards has denied those accusations but has admitted to at times making staff feel uncomfortable.

GOP LAWMAKER'S GIFTS, 'EFFUSIVE AFFECTION' TOWARD YOUNG STAFFERS DETAILED IN EXPLOSIVE ETHICS REPORT

And Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, has been accused of domestic abuse by his ex-wife and former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, and is facing pressure from congressional Republicans to drop out of his race as well. One House GOP source called the situation a "f---ing trainwreck" in comments to Fox News Digital.

Miller has denied any wrongdoing and asked the House Ethics Committee to initiate an investigation in order to clear his name. The former Trump aide has resisted calls to exit the race, insisting he will win in November and that the public accusations from his ex-wife are a bid to derail his political career.

All three House seats are on the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) target list, meaning Democrats are pouring money and resources into those races.

One House Republican, who was granted anonymity to speak freely, told Fox News Digital that all three should drop out of their races, stating, "We must lead by example."

Mills' primary debate is Wednesday night.

item.title: Political newcomer seeks to unseat twin of Trump impeachment foe in swing Virginia district
item.description: Three GOP political newcomers battled it out in Virginia 7th Congressional District to challenge Rep. Eugene Vindman, twin brother of Trump impeachment witness Alexander Vindman.
item.content:encoded:
Douglas Ollivant decisively beat two fellow political newcomers in the Republican primary contest to take on incumbent Rep. Eugene Vindman, D-Va., in November.

Vindman, whose twin brother is a high-profile foe of President Donald Trump, currently represents Virginia's 7th Congressional district, a seat previously held by the state's Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger.

The Republican primary race between Ollivant, Rick Smithers and Philip Harding was unique in that none of the candidates had held elected office before, though two have government experience. The lack of reliable polling made it difficult to foretell who would emerge triumphant — but Ollivant ran away with victory, earning 56.6% of the vote compared to Harding's 30.7% and Smithers' 12.8%. 

THE BALLOT BOX SHOWDOWNS THIS MONTH THAT YOU NEED TO WATCH

Ollivant is a retired Army officer who served as the National Security Council director for Iraq during the George W. Bush administration. He worked as a national security analyst and consultant after that.

Smithers is a pastor and construction business owner who branded himself as the biggest outsider in the race.

Harding is a businessman with a bachelor's degree from Harvard University. He also earned his graduate degree from the Harvard Kennedy School of Government.

All three candidates have generally aligned themselves with Donald Trump, though the president did not endorse anyone in the race.

FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: DEMOCRATS LEAD IN THE HOUSE, BUT REDISTRICTING KEEPS THE GOP IN THE GAME

According to FEC data, Ollivant had the cash advantage, raising $251,134. Harding raised $125,916 before primary Election Day, and there was no reported fundraising data for Smithers.

Virginia's 7th Congressional District, located in the northeastern part of the state and encompassing Culpeper and Fredericksburg east into Stafford, Spotsylvania, Caroline and parts of Prince William County, is considered a true swing state.

Vindman, who ran unopposed this time around, won the vacant seat by only three points.

SCOOP: HOUSE REPUBLICANS TARGET DOZENS OF VULNERABLE DEMOCRATS ON EVE OF TAX FILING DEADLINE

As Democrats hope to retain the seat in November, Republicans are eyeing it as a potential flip, which would be a welcome pickup as the GOP fights tooth-and-nail to keep control of Congress, a historically difficult feat for the party in power during a midterm election year.

Vindman's twin brother Alexander is a longtime foe of Trump. Alexander Vindman is a former military official, and the then-National Security Council director for European affairs testified against Trump during the first failed impeachment attempt in 2019.

Alexander is an ardent defender of Ukraine, and became a central figure of the impeachment attempt, claiming that in a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump attempted to make military aid for the embattled European nation contingent on an investigation into the Biden family's involvement in Ukrainian business activities.

Ultimately, the impeachment failed, and both Alexander and Eugene Vindman were removed from the National Security Council.

Alexander Vindman later became a frequent anti-Trump guest on CNN and MSNBC, as well as on the left-wing podcast circuit.

item.title: Secret FBI probe cast Trump as possible Russian asset after Comey firing, memos show
item.description: Declassified FBI memos reveal the bureau opened a counterintelligence probe codenamed "Oxferd Comma" after Trump fired James Comey in 2017.
item.content:encoded:
The White House released newly declassified FBI memos showing that the bureau opened a 2017 counterintelligence investigation into whether President Donald Trump’s firing of James Comey was connected to Russia.

The investigation, codenamed "Oxferd Comma," opened after Trump fired FBI Director James Comey in May 2017, according to the White House's release. It is unclear as to why the word "Oxford" was seemingly misspelled.

The probe was launched due to national security concerns about whether Trump himself was a Russian asset, the documents allege.

Investigators sought to determine whether Trump was "directed by, controlled by, and/or coordinated activities with, the Russian Federation in a manner constituting a threat to the national security of the United States and/or a violation of federal criminal statutes," according an FBI memo on May 16, 2017, jump-starting the investigation.

"In addition, this investigation will also seek to determine whether President Trump and others yet to be named obstructed and/or conspiracy to obstruct any associated FBI investigation," the same memo added.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for additional comment on Wednesday. 

This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

item.title: Shaquille O'Neal talks LeBron James' Lakers legacy, why his new 76ers might be extremely 'dangerous'
item.description: Shaquille O'Neal ranks LeBron James in the Lakers hierarchy and raises concerns about the Philadelphia 76ers' ball-sharing with Joel Embiid.
item.content:encoded:
In an unprecedented 24th season in the NBA, LeBron James will try to make even more history with his new fourth team.

James signed a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers late last month, joining a team with newly acquired Jaylen Brown, one-time MVP Joel Embiid and scoring machine Tyrese Maxey to make them a championship contender in the Eastern Conference.

No player has ever won an NBA title with four separate teams (James is one of four players to win with three, along with John Salley, Robert Horry and Danny Green), but before James tries to bring one to Philly for the first time since 1983, his Los Angeles Lakers legacy is already a hot topic.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

James helped the Lakers win the 2020 NBA title in the Disney "bubble" for his fourth title, for each of which he was named the Finals MVP. That is enough, Shaquille O'Neal says, to be considered a Lakers great.

"He definitely won a championship there and was a big game player, so he’s in the building," O'Neal told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

But he stopped short of putting him in the "top floor."

"Top floor belongs to Magic (Johnson), Kobe (Bryant), and Kareem (Abdul-Jabbar). I’m going to put Kareem," O'Neal continued. "The second floor is me and those other guys.

NBA GREAT SAYS HE NEARLY 'DROPPED DEAD' DUE TO BLOOD CLOT AS HE OFFERS ADVICE TO VICTOR WEMBANYAMA

"Kobe and Magic played there longer than I did, and Magic was the first guy to bring that 'set.' LeBron will probably always be under those guys, but that doesn't take away from what he’s done in the game."

While discussing the timeless James, O'Neal recalled his timeless memories of eating Lucky Charms, as the self-dubbed cereal expert will be helping "the biggest cereal fan" win cash prizes, a hangout with the Big Diesel and more through General Mills' latest contest.

"I eat cereal because it brings out the kid in me," the newest General Mills partner said. "It’s what I like to do when I’m watching movies; last night, I was watching "Stranger Things Chapter 3," and it came on so perfect I had to pause it and go in there and get me some Lucky Charms, buddy. A big bowl, too. I came back in, turned my light on, turned the AC down to make it colder in the room, and hit play; it just made me feel like a kid because I’ve always been a Lucky Charms fan.

"Even though I’m 54, when I get home by myself and I’m watching a movie, I like to take it back to when I was age nine or 10 where mom and dad were sleeping. I’d go downstairs, get a nice bowl of cereal, and I'd have to wash the bowl before they got up so nobody knew I had my bowl of cereal... Teaming up with General Mills was a perfect fit because I’ve been eating these cereals forever."

The one thing about James' move to the City of Brotherly Love, however, is that there is, in fact, just one basketball.

"If you look at that roster, it could be a legendary or dangerous roster. The dangerous part is I’m worried about Maxey and Brown, because Embiid is going to want the ball, and LeBron loves having the ball. Brown and Maxey are both used to having the ball deep into the shot clock to get into their shot. With LeBron holding the ball and Embiid wanting it in the post, them getting only two or three seconds with the shot clock is a different game. I don't know if they are going to be ready for that," O'Neal said.

item.title: Astros player belts home run, rounds the bases and then gets devastating news after touching home
item.description: Taylor Trammell's head-down home run trot at Daikin Park turned into an embarrassing moment when the ball was caught at the wall against Toronto.
item.content:encoded:
Houston Astros outfielder Taylor Trammell took a useless jog around the bases in a game against the Toronto Blue Jays earlier this week.

Talk about a brutal plot twist.

Trammell belted what he thought was his sixth home run of the season in the seventh inning of Monday's eventual loss to Toronto. The lefty uncorked on a fastball to the deepest part of Daikin Park (should still be Minute Maid Park, but that's neither here nor there), and thought he got all of it.

He touched first, rounded second, hit third and then finished his trot by touching home, thanking God, and making the short, triumphant walk back to his dugout for a well-earned congratulations from the rest of the team.

The only problem? When he finally looked up for the obligatory "atta boys!" from his teammates, they were nowhere to be found ...

... Because the ball was caught at the wall.

Take a look:

Oh no! Just a brutal look for Taylor Trammell. Humiliating. Devastating. I can't even imagine what's going through his head when he touches home and then realizes what he just did.

How do you look your teammates in the eyes after that jog? Goodness. Better yet, how do they look him in the eyes after?

Do they laugh? Do they try to pick him up? Do they just ignore it and act like it never happened? What a pickle.

To be fair, Trammell was clearly locked in. Good for him, by the way. We always rag on guys who show up the pitcher and make a huge spectacle out of hitting a home run.

Trammell put his head down and ran hard. That's what we want, right? No showboating. No bat-flipping. No admiring his blast. Just put your head down, touch all the bases, and get back to the dugout.

You're down 3-0. It's not the time for showing off.

item.title: Perez Hilton under involuntary psych hold after apparent self-harm livestream: source
item.description: Miami-Dade deputies responded to Perez Hilton's home after receiving multiple reports about an apparent self-harm incident during a TikTok livestream.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Law enforcement was called to Perez Hilton's Miami residence after the celebrity blogger appeared to be harming himself during a TikTok livestream on Tuesday evening.

"The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office received multiple calls regarding an individual who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media," a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Deputies quickly located the individual’s residence, where they spoke with family members on scene, and confirmed he was alone inside."

"In many incidents involving a person experiencing a mental health crisis or actively harming themselves, deputies prioritize de-escalation by creating time, distance, and opportunities for communication. Unless there is an immediate threat to others, slowing the situation and utilizing crisis intervention techniques can reduce the likelihood of a suicide-by-cop encounter and minimize the risk of injury to the individual, deputies, and the public."

CELEBRITY BLOGGER PEREZ HILTON SAYS HE FOUND GOD AMID MEDICAL SCARE IN EMOTIONAL CONFESSION

"At this time, deputies have tactically disengaged while continuing to monitor the situation and providing the needed support to his family," the statement concludes. 

A source close to the situation tells Fox News Digital that Hilton was placed under a psychiatric hold under the Baker Act and "had wounds and cuts all over the place." 

"He’s alive," the source added. "He has superficial cuts all over the body."

The Florida Baker Act is a state law that gives law enforcement officers, judges and certain mental health professionals the authority to place an individual into an involuntary mental health evaluation when specific legal criteria are met. 

Under the Baker Act, an individual can be transported to a designated receiving facility for an emergency psychiatric evaluation that generally lasts up to 72 hours.

A representative for Hilton did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. 

The content creator recently moved to Miami with his mother, 73, and his three young children.

Hilton, born Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr., rose to fame in the mid-2000s after launching his celebrity gossip website in 2004. The Miami native quickly became one of the internet's most influential entertainment voices, known for breaking celebrity news and his unfiltered commentary.

The media personality has frequently shared how parenthood has reshaped his priorities, often offering followers a glimpse into family life on social media.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Earlier this year, Hilton revealed he had been hospitalized for 21 days after a severe case of sepsis stemming from complications related to the flu. The celebrity blogger said he developed an ulcer and stomach perforation after taking medication on an empty stomach, ultimately requiring emergency surgery and weeks of treatment.

In a candid video he shared at the time, he said God had "presented himself to me" during the ordeal and changed him through the experience.

"God presented himself to me and then did something. Something I can only call miraculous... it was real, and this has been life-changing," he said.

In a follow-up video, the entertainment columnist tearfully apologized for past mistakes and said he had begun reading the Bible again.

"I’ve been crying, but happy tears. Happy tears. Because this is just, this is just so crazy. I’ve been reading the Bible, and so much of what is said here I had already been thinking of. It’s just overwhelming in the best, most beautiful way," he said while holding up a Bible to the camera.

"I made a lot of mistakes in my past. We all have. Nobody's perfect," he said. "But my mistakes are very public. The internet is forever. Receipts are forever. I carry with me deep shame and regret. I'm sorry. I will continue to apologize. I have also reached out to make amends. I've apologized publicly and privately to dozens of people."

"Because I was so selfish, because I didn't care who I hurt. I just cared about the views, the attention, the money — people hated me," he continued. "Some people enjoyed it, but it felt like most people hated me. And last week, since I've been home, I haven't been getting as much hate, and I've been getting love and prayers."

Hilton added, "And I know that some people are fed up with me talking about God. You don’t have to watch these videos. You don’t have to watch. I love God. My experience was real. My testimony is important."

"What matters is today. How I behave today, how I behave tomorrow," he continued. "And not only did God save me in so many ways, but God gave me a new lease on life and a new opportunity to truly be better and do better."

Fox News Digital's Kristine Parks contributed to this post.

item.title: Fake party invitation scam can hijack your computer
item.description: Fake party invitations trick victims into downloading malware that gives criminals remote access to computers and spreads through contact lists.
item.content:encoded:
You sit down at your computer to clear out your inbox. Then you spot a party invitation from someone you recognize. Maybe it appears to come from a friend. Perhaps the sender belongs to a group you know. Either way, the familiar name makes the message feel safe enough to open.

Inside, everything looks cheerful. There is an envelope graphic, a friendly note and what appears to be an invitation for a wedding or retirement party. However, you cannot see the event details yet. The message tells you to save the invitation or install something to join the guest list.

That request should stop you cold. A legitimate party invitation should not require you to install software before you can see when or where the event takes place. That small download could give a criminal remote access to your computer. Here’s how this fake invitation scam works and what you can do before one click puts your computer and contacts at risk.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE SHINYHUNTERS SEXTORTION EMAIL USES CARNIVAL BREACH DATA

The scam begins with trust. An invitation appears to come from someone whose name you recognize, so you become less suspicious. Criminals may copy the look of a legitimate invitation platform. They can add a colorful envelope, an exclusive-sounding message and a button that promises to reveal the details.

The email has one main purpose: getting you to click. Once you press the invitation, the message sends you to a separate website. That page says a friend sent you something and asks you to download a file to view it.

The request may seem simple. Still, party invitations normally open inside a website or app. They do not need to install a program on your computer.

The landing page may contain a large "Download invitation" button. It may also display a familiar company name inside the web address. However, seeing a trusted brand somewhere in a link proves very little. Criminals can place that name inside a much longer address or add extra letters that make the domain look authentic at a glance.

You need to identify the real domain instead of focusing on the first familiar word you see. The page may also create confusion. It could claim that your invitation is already downloading while another message asks you to click if the download fails. Some versions even include a testimonial from a supposed guest who says opening the invitation was easy.

A review on a private party invitation page should feel strange. Those details are designed to quiet your doubts and push you toward the download button. For more visual breakdowns of scams like this, check out The CyberGuy Report podcast at CyberGuy.com.

In the example we describe, the website directs you to open the file on a Windows computer. That device-specific request is another major warning sign. Why would a party invitation care which device you use? The malicious file may contain a remote access tool. Businesses use legitimate versions of this software to troubleshoot computers from another location.

Criminals can abuse similar tools to control your system without permission. Once you install the file, an attacker may be able to search your computer or access saved information. The exact damage depends on the program and the permissions it receives. Your email account can become an especially valuable target. It contains personal conversations along with a contact list filled with people who trust you.

The criminals can then send the same fake invitation to your friends and relatives. Those people may open it because the message appears to come from your real account. As a result, one compromised computer can start a chain reaction.

People receive a steady stream of spam, fake alerts and impersonation attempts. Criminals can also use AI tools to create cleaner writing and more realistic designs. That makes the familiar sender name even more powerful.

You may be cautious around a message from a stranger. Yet you might act quickly when the invitation appears to come from someone you know. The scam succeeds when familiarity replaces verification. Email providers and technology companies continue to improve their filters. Even so, dangerous messages still reach real inboxes. That leaves you making the final decision about whether a link deserves your trust.

HOTEL WI-FI PHISHING ATTACK TARGETS MICROSOFT LOGINS

A few precautions can help you recognize a malicious invitation before it compromises your computer or accounts.

Use strong antivirus software and keep it actively running in the background on your devices. Real-time protection can warn you about a dangerous link or block a malicious download before it reaches your computer.

If you clicked the invitation or downloaded a suspicious file, delete the file without opening it and run a full security scan. A scan can help identify unwanted software that may have reached your computer. Keep your operating system, browser and security software updated as well. Updates often close weaknesses that criminals try to exploit. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com

Stop immediately if an invitation tells you to download or install a program before you can see the event. Real invitation services normally show the details in your browser or inside their official app. You should not need a separate installer. Delete the message instead of trying to see what happens next.

On a computer, place your cursor over a link without pressing it. Your browser or email program should reveal the destination address. Read the entire address carefully. Watch for misspellings, unexpected words or extra letters added around a legitimate company name. A familiar logo does not confirm that the link belongs to the real company.

Avoid using the link inside the email when you have doubts. Instead, type the invitation service's web address into your browser or open its official app. Sign in and look for the invitation there. If it does not appear in your account, the email may be fake.

Reach out through a separate text message or phone call if an invitation feels unusual. Do not reply directly to the suspicious email. A criminal may control the sender's account or may have forged the address. Ask whether the person actually sent the invitation and whether it requires a download.

FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK

Your risk is generally lower if you visited the page but did not run anything. Close the browser tab without pressing the download button. If the file has already downloaded, leave it closed and delete it. Opening the file gives the malicious program a chance to run. Never open it simply to find out what it contains.

Use your email provider's Report phishing option before deleting the invitation. Reporting the message can help the provider block similar emails and warn other recipients. You can also block the sender if you do not recognize the address.

A data removal service can help remove your details from many public data broker databases. This may make it harder for scammers to find personal information they can use to make a message feel convincing. However, no service can remove every record. It also cannot prevent a criminal from reaching you through a compromised friend's contact list. Still, reducing your public exposure can give scammers less material to work with. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) for your email account. This adds another barrier if criminals steal or guess your password. Never approve an unexpected login request. Also, do not share a security code with anyone who contacts you.

If you typed your email address, password or security code into the fake page, use a clean device to change that password immediately. Change it anywhere else you reused it. Then review the account for unfamiliar activity, new recovery information or settings you did not change. Use a password manager to create and store a strong, unique password for every account so one stolen login cannot unlock several services.

Disconnect the computer from the internet if you ran the installer or noticed unexpected remote activity. Next, run a full security scan. You may also need help from a trusted computer professional to confirm that the remote access software is gone. Use a different, clean device to change important passwords. Start with your email account because criminals may use it to reset passwords for other services. Also, review your email account for unfamiliar forwarding rules or active login sessions. Warn your contacts if suspicious messages may have gone out under your name.

A party invitation should give you information, not demand access to your computer. Delete the message if it asks you to install anything before revealing the event. Check the full destination of every link. Then contact the supposed sender separately when something feels unusual. If you downloaded a file but did not open it, delete it and run a security scan. If you ran the file, disconnect the computer and secure your accounts from a clean device. Most importantly, pay attention to that moment when something feels off. A few seconds of doubt can stop a criminal from getting inside your computer. Want to see more? Check out The CyberGuy Report podcast.

Should email providers face tougher requirements to stop malicious invitations before they ever reach your inbox? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Dems' leftward lurch gets legs as El-Sayed's Michigan Senate victory sparks party debate
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's win over Haley Stevens in the Michigan Senate primary hands Republicans like Mike Rogers fresh ammunition in a crucial battleground.
item.content:encoded:
DETROIT, MI - Abdul El-Sayed's victory over moderate Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's high-stakes Democratic Senate primary is a massive boost for the party's left-wing in its ideological battle with the center-left establishment.

The win called Wednesday morning gives instant ammunition to Republicans aiming to flip a crucial battleground Senate seat the Democrats must hold as part of their midterm push to win back control of the chamber.

Republican nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers, in a Fox News Digital interview ahead of the primary, argued that El-Sayed is "way too extreme for Michigan. I mean, Abdul, he has his own special sauce of crazy."

MEET THE FAR LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN THE 2026 MIDTERMS

El-Sayed is a far-left figure backed by progressive champions and socialists like Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and other members of the "Squad." He beat Stevens, an establishment Democrat, by 1% when the race was called by AP with 99% of the vote counted on Wednesday morning.

A former Wayne County Health Department director, El-Sayed, if elected in November, would make history as the nation's first Muslim senator. He is an epidemiologist who unsuccessfully ran for governor as an insurgent candidate in 2018. He has made support for "Medicare-for-all" a major component of his campaign.

He has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and is a vocal critic of Israel amid its war with Hamas — even characterizing Israel's actions in Gaza as "genocide" against Palestinians. El-Sayed, who served as a top surrogate on Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, has also vowed not to accept PAC donations.

El-Sayed's primary election victory has some wondering if the party of the late Rep. John Dingell, who was famously known as the "Dean of the House" during his historic tenure in Congress, and his wife Rep. Debbie Dingell, the current dean of the Michigan congressional delegation, has broadly shifted to the left, or if this is a one-off election dynamic.

MIKE ROGERS ARGUES ABDUL EL-SAYED IS 'A SPECIAL SAUCE OF CRAZY'

"It’s not all that clear that the party has shifted that far to the left," Matt Bennett, one of the leaders at the Third Way, a leading center-left Democratic organization, told Fox News Digital.

Pointing to the increasing visceral opposition to President Donald Trump by Democrats across the country, Bennett said the primary results in Michigan may be "a unique situation where candidates matter."

"And in this moment Democratic voters everywhere are very very angry at Trump and they’re flipping over the tables and taking it out on the establishment and Haley, for better or worse, has run as the establishment."

Matt Grossmann, director of the Institute for Public Policy and Social Research and political science professor at Michigan State University, pointed to what he called a "recruitment failure."

"Stevens was no one’s first choice," Grossmann said of Stevens, as he referred to unsuccessful efforts to recruit term-limited Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer or former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg to launch a campaign in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Noting growing opposition among Democrats nationwide to Israel's ongoing military operations against Hamas in Gaza, and the massive amounts of outside money spent in the historically expensive Senate primary by groups aligned with pro-Israel interests to help Stevens and target El-Sayed, Grossmann added, "This was a terrible year to be running the most pro-Israel candidate available."

More than $80 million was spent on the primary, making it the most expensive Democratic Senate nomination contest in history. Much of the money came from outside groups supporting Stevens or opposing El-Sayed. The largest spender was United Democracy Project, a political action committee aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which is best known by its acronym AIPAC.

El-Sayed said his victory is easy to understand.

Speaking with Fox News Digital on Sunday, he said "our job is to listen to folks, as it has been since we kicked off this campaign... to understand the challenges people have in their lives."

"I think the people are telling us that they want money out of politics. Money in your pocket, Medicare-for-all," he emphasized. "You know, endorsements don't vote. People vote. And I think right now people are voting with their feet."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Adam Green, co-founder of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee (PCCC), a leading group on the left, referred to El-Sayed's narrow margin over Stevens and told Fox News Digital that "any win against $60 million of outside spending by AIPAC and corporate interests is a giant win and sets us on a path of proving our case in November to shake up the system."

The progressive-versus-establishment battle also played out in Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, a Republican-controlled swing seat that is among roughly two dozen races expected to help determine control of the House.

William Lawrence, a co-founder of the Sunrise Movement climate advocacy group, edged out two more moderate Democrats. Lawrence was backed by Sanders and El-Sayed, as well as several prominent progressive groups. He will face Republican Rep. Tom Barrett in the general election.

The party’s internal battle was also on display in Michigan’s heavily Democratic 13th Congressional District, where the Associated Press had not projected a winner early Wednesday.

Rep. Shri Thanedar, who is supported by top House Democratic leaders, was being challenged by state Rep. Donovan McKinney. McKinney was backed by Sanders, El-Sayed and "Squad" members Reps. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts and Summer Lee of Pennsylvania.

Bennett noted that Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan crushed a more progressive rival in the 2024 Senate primary before winning the general election by a razor-thin margin over Rogers in a state that President Donald Trump narrowly carried.

And Bennett and Grossmann pointed out that Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, who won the Democratic gubernatorial primary on Tuesday, and Attorney General Dana Nessel, who was renominated, are far from left-wingers.

"The party hasn’t shifted far to the left but this particular primary did," Bennett argued, as he referred to El-Sayed's victory over Stevens.

item.title: McConnell's absence puts Trump agenda at risk as Kentucky succession questions grow
item.description: Andy Beshear says the Aug. 3 deadline has no legal impact on his options, but Mitch McConnell's absence leaves Republicans one vote short on key items.
item.content:encoded:
A deadline that could have determined Sen. Mitch McConnell’s future in the Senate has come and gone as the timeline for the Kentucky Republican’s return remains in the air.

Speculation swirled over Aug. 3 and its ramifications for McConnell’s winnowing tenure in the Senate, given that he’s been absent from the public eye since early June and is slated to retire at the end of this year.

Armchair election quarterbacks suggested that Monday was the day for Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, a Democrat, to have called a special election to replace McConnell.

MCCONNELL OUT OF HOSPITAL, STILL NOT 'MEDICALLY CLEARED' TO RETURN TO SENATE

But the longtime Republican has not vacated his seat, and Beshear contended that the obscure deadline had no real legal teeth.

"I know there are a lot of folks wondering about the significance of August 3 regarding a potential Senate vacancy," Beshear said on X. "I want everyone to know that this date has no legal impact on my options should there be a vacancy this year."

Still, Kentucky’s Senate succession law has undergone major changes in recent years. Should the Bluegrass State suddenly have a vacant seat in the upper chamber, Beshear wouldn’t be allowed to appoint a replacement as is the case in other states — this was most recently put to the test when Sen. Lindsey Graham suddenly died in South Carolina.

COLLINS DROPS THE HAMMER ON TRUMP'S PICK TO LEAD DOJ, JEOPARDIZING PATH TO CONFIRMATION

That means if McConnell’s seat were to become vacant, Beshear would be required to call a special election to fill his remaining time in the Senate.

When asked for comment on the matter, McConnell’s office directed Fox News Digital to the last statement from the senator, released on July 27, that detailed under doctors' orders that he was not "medically cleared" to return to the Senate quite yet. 

"I’m still working hard to get back to my full schedule of work in the Senate and in Kentucky, keeping up with intense physical therapy per my doctors’ orders," McConnell said.

Despite the acknowledgment that Monday meant little legally when it came to replacing McConnell, Beshear noted that his absence is hindering current and future agenda items for the Trump administration.

"Worth a reminder: Right now, there’s one less vote for the SAVE Act, Trump’s war with Iran, or the potential replacement of a SCOTUS justice," he said.

TRUMP KEEPS CALLING THUNE DESPITE PUBLIC FIGHT OVER SAVE AMERICA ACT

And the Senate is chugging along without the longest-serving Republican leader in history. However, his missing dozens of votes hasn’t necessarily stopped legislation so far.

But during the dizzying sprint to wrap up work ahead of a scheduled break during August, his vote could count more than ever.

There are three Republicans who are on the fence about Blanche, too.

Notably, President Donald Trump’s nomination of acting Attorney General Todd Blanche is hanging by a thread, in part, because McConnell is not there. Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, announced her intention to vote against him, leaving Republicans with only one vote to spare before his path to leading the Department of Justice closes.

"I don't know what those individuals are going to do, and I just… Mitch is still out," Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., told Fox News Digital. "But I think he’ll be confirmed. And we've got a lot of work to do this week."

item.title: Angels vs Orioles preview with player prop picks and under 8 runs analysis
item.description: Reid Detmers faces Trevor Rogers as the Los Angeles Angels and Baltimore Orioles clash in a post-deadline matchup with more trades likely ahead.
item.content:encoded:
It is a getaway day for most teams as we have every team in baseball playing, and most will end their series today. This has been a week of a lot of travel for many baseball players with the trade deadline finishing on Monday. Interestingly enough, that isn't the last chance for players to be moved.

Virtually all teams put their players on the market, and if someone claims or tries to trade for them from here, they just take the player off the market. Odd concept, but that's what happens. You can expect the two teams in this one to explore who wants what remains of the Los Angeles Angels and Baltimore Orioles over the next couple of months.

The Angels did something right! At least that is what the majority of the analysts are saying about their trade deadline deals. They received some key pieces and didn't sacrifice a ton of their own young talent in the process. They picked up the second-best prospect from the Toronto Blue Jays in a deal sending over Jose Soriano. Moises Ballesteros came over to them from the Cubs for a reliever. They were able to keep Zach Neto and, if it is important to you, Mike Trout.

Another person they kept on the squad was today's starter Reid Detmers. There were a lot of rumors about people wanting to get Detmers from the Angels, but he ultimately stayed with the club, and they can trade him another year if they want. This season hasn't been amazing based on some numbers - he has a 3-7 record, with a 4.03 ERA, and a 1.10 WHIP. The WHIP is a good indicator of his performance, and he also ranks ninth in strikeouts. I also think they are likely to unleash him a bit more now that the deadline has passed. He was limited to fewer than 90 pitches in each of the past four starts. Detmers has been good against the Orioles, holding them to just seven hits in 40 at-bats.

The Orioles seem to have pressed the reset button. They aren't in the same situation as the Angels because they are roughly a .500 team, but that won't cut it in the American League East. It is also highly unlikely they can make a push for a wild card spot with their pitching staff.

The team still has a ton of talent on the roster, but they did trade away Adley Rutschman to the Boston Red Sox. It is more surprising to me that they traded him to a divisional opponent than it was that they traded him.

In my opinion, they still needed to make more moves to help this pitching staff. Their second-best starter, Trevor Rogers takes today's start. In my opinion, Rogers is closer to a third starter at his best than he is the second in a playoff-caliber team. For the year, he is 6-7 with a 4.27 ERA and a 1.28 WHIP. He had a solid July aside from a rough outing against the Tigers in his last start. Over the last two months, he has allowed 15 earned runs in 60 innings, which is probably peak performance from him. The Angels are hitting just 8-for-22 against Rogers, but Travis d'Arnaud is 7-for-15 against him.

item.title: DSA-backed candidate topples millionaire Dem incumbent
item.description: DSA-backed Donavan McKinney unseated Rep. Shri Thanedar in Michigan's 13th district Democratic primary, extending a wave of socialist wins nationwide.
item.content:encoded:
Donavan McKinney, a congressional candidate backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) in Michigan’s 13th Congressional District, won his Democratic primary on Wednesday morning, unseating incumbent Rep. Shri Thanedar, D-Mich.

From primary candidates in New York like socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier and her victory over incumbent Rep. Adriano Espillat, D-N.Y., the veteran chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, to Melat Kiros, another socialist in Colorado, unseating 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette, D-Colo., DSA-backed candidates have expanded their influence over the party.

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

They’ve even enjoyed victories over other progressives — like Thanedar.

Thanedar, while still a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, has broken with the DSA on a few critical areas.

Most notably, Thanedar broke off his own membership with the DSA in October 2023 over his support for Israel.

"I can no longer associate with an organization unwilling to call out terrorism in all its forms. Sunday’s hate-filled and antisemitic rally in New York City, promoted by the NYC-DSA, makes it impossible for me to continue my affiliation. I stand with Israel and its right to defend itself," Thanedar wrote in a statement after the Oct. 7 terror attacks that left 1,200 Israelis dead.  

Right before the Fourth of July, Rep. Thanedar also said he agreed with U.S. exceptionalism when asked whether he was proud to be an American.

FORMER BERNIE SANDERS OFFICIAL ACCUSES SENATOR OF PUSHING MOST ANTISEMITIC CANDIDATES 'IN A GENERATION'

"This is a great country. You know, we are a country of immigrants. Immigrants have contributed so much to our country, and you know this is the greatest country on earth. I am so proud to call myself an American citizen, although there are some concerns with the new administration," Thanedar said.

McKinney, for his own part, has listed affordability, environmental and climate justice, and getting money out of politics as among his top priorities.

During his campaign, he targeted Thanedar’s personal wealth, arguing the businessman wasn’t representative of his district’s lived experience. Thanedar bought a small chemical analysis lab in 1991 for $75,000, grew it into a multimillion-dollar business with multiple acquisitions, later founding and then selling Avomeen Analytical Services, a chemical testing company.

"We deserve a Democratic Party that leads the fight against the billionaires that are robbing us blind. That stands up to corporate PACs. Our country and our children can afford nothing less," McKinney said in a campaign video.

DEMS CLASH OVER AIPAC MONEY, ‘OGRE’ ATTACK AND ELECTABILITY DURING CRUCIAL SENATE DEBATE

"People like our congressman, Shri Thanedar, are the problem. A multimillionaire who spent millions to buy a seat in Congress, who has more in common with Donald Trump and Elon Musk than people like us."

Having captured the Democratic nomination, McKinney will go on to the general election on Nov. 3.

JELLY ROLL'S WIFE BUNNIE XO BREAKS SILENCE ON DIVORCE, GETS EMOTIONAL ABOUT FINAL FIGHT

item.title: Republicans get the Democrat they wanted as socialist Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Haley Stevens in a bruising Michigan Democratic primary, but his progressive stances give Mike Rogers ammunition ahead of November.
item.content:encoded:
After a grueling, messy campaign, a far-left progressive has taken on the Democratic establishment and won.

Abdul El-Sayed felled Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., to secure the Democratic nomination for Senate in what became one of the ugliest Democratic primary races in the country. El-Sayed will now face former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers, who was uncontested in the GOP primary, in November.

Big money, the Democratic old guard and attacks on El-Sayed’s Democratic Socialist leanings dominated the primary, and leave the last man standing on the Left bruised and battered heading into the showdown with Rogers.

The face-off to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters, who backed Stevens, is a must-win contest for Democrats and one of roughly a dozen general election Senate races expected to determine whether Republicans retain their narrow majority.

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

"Michigan... We won. I am so proud to be your Democratic nominee for US Senate. Let's win in November," El Sayed wrote in a social media post Wednesday morning, as he declared victory.

A couple of hours later, after the race was called, Stevens conceded:  "I love Michigan and am so proud to have put up my hand to serve. I spoke with Abdul a few moments ago to offer him my full support as we work to defeat Mike Rogers this November."

At a news conference, El-Sayed preached unity.

"To my colleague and friend, Congresswoman Haley Stevens. We shared a great conversation this morning, and I know that it was a bitter end to this very long primary," he said. "But I also know that Haley brings, the best of herself to her work. She is one of the most committed public servants that you'll ever meet. she loves democracy. Like, I love democracy and whatever differences that we might have had in the primary, they pale in comparison to what unifies us."

And as a Senate Republican-aligned group instantly fired up an attack ad on El-Sayed using old controversial comments, he took aim at Rogers.

"As bitter and as divisive and as cynical as the campaign against us might have been, I want us to realize that there is so much more that unites us now, because the campaign that Mike Rogers and Donald Trump and their GOP MAGA allies are launching is already more bitter," he argued. "All you got to do is look at the ads you're already watching on TV that started today. You know, they think they want to use my whole name against me. Mike. Listen, man, if you can't say the name, it's Abdulrahman. Keep the name out of your damn mouth."

But even before Primary Day, El-Sayed was already looking ahead to his battle with Rogers, and hoping to curry favor with Stevens’ voters in the process.

"I think we all understand the risk of Donald Trump. We all understand the risk of Mike Rogers," El-Sayed told Fox News Digital. "This is a guy who is not going to stand up and take on the war machine. He's not going to stand up and take on Big Pharma. He's not going to stand up and take on big tech."

"He is going to do the bidding of large corporations," he continued. "I think everybody understands what the stakes are. So I'm looking forward to welcoming everybody who might have voted differently in the primary."

SWING-STATE POLL SPELLS TROUBLE FOR FAR LEFT AS SCHUMER-BACKED CANDIDATE DOMINATES WITH CRITICAL VOTING BLOCS

El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and a former Wayne County health director who unsuccessfully ran for governor as an insurgent candidate in 2018, would become the nation’s first Muslim senator if elected. He has made support for "Medicare for All" a major component of his campaign.

He has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and has been a vocal critic of Israel during its war against Hamas, characterizing Israel’s actions in Gaza as "genocide" against Palestinians.

More than $80 million was spent on the primary, making it the most expensive Democratic Senate nomination contest in history. Much of the money came from outside groups supporting Stevens or opposing El-Sayed. The largest spender was United Democracy Project, a political action committee aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which is best known by its acronym AIPAC.

"We all knew that they were going to spend their money. We didn't know they were going to spend $70 million of their money. We didn't know that they were going to outspend us $11 to $1. And yet we're still standing," El-Sayed highlighted in his speech.

El-Sayed urged party unity and took aim at former Rep. Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate nominee.

Stevens also targeted Rogers during her primary night speech.

"Whoever wins is going to go and take on Mike Rogers. Republicans are going to do everything they can to throw all the dirt, all the mud, the kitchen sink at us because they want to keep the U.S. Senate red, so Mike Rogers can keep rubber-stamping Donald Trump's ridiculous agenda," she argued.

Of the two candidates, Republicans wanted El-Sayed, and old-guard Democrats feared his victory the most. The GOP is leaning into the bloody primary, too, hoping that the battle damage will have staying power in the weeks ahead until November. 

"Not only is Rogers a battle-tested candidate who has coalesced the support of Michigan’s entire GOP ecosystem, but he will also be the beneficiary of Democrats’ dysfunction come November," a Republican operative told Fox News Digital. "Abdul El-Sayed has emerged from this cycle’s Democratic primary more damaged than ever and susceptible to more onslaughts of criticism from within their own party."

His surge in the polls sent Democrats scrambling to back Stevens, forcing Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer and Peters off the sidelines.

Peters told Fox News Digital that Stevens was a proven winner who had previously flipped a red district to blue, and that ultimately, the main goal was recapturing control of the Senate.

"But it doesn't happen if we lose Michigan," Peters said.

DEMS CLASH OVER AIPAC MONEY, ‘OGRE’ ATTACK AND ELECTABILITY DURING CRUCIAL SENATE DEBATE

Stevens acknowledged the former in an interview with Fox News Digital, where she said, "Rogers has made it very clear that, you know, this gets easier if I am not the nominee."

That’s because Republicans are leaning into El-Sayed being the more "extreme" of the two over his staunch opposition to U.S. aid for Israel, nixing corporate money in elections and pushing Medicare for all, which have all been underscored by his prior comments to defund police and recent "ogre on a pike" gaffe.

Still, his policy positions are hallmarks of the progressive movement that have earned him endorsements from the likes of Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.

And his victory marks another loss for Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., who backed Stevens in her failed bid to claim the Democratic nomination. 

"Abdul El-Sayed’s victory marks another devastating loss for Chuck Schumer in his civil war with Bernie Sanders as Democrats position Mike Rogers to defeat socialism’s newest standard-bearer in November," National Republican Senatorial Committee spokeswoman Bernadette Breslin told Fox News Digital.

Rogers was game for either, but did toss a jab in at El-Sayed in an interview with Fox News Digital.

"We feel confident we're going to beat either one of those candidates that come out of that race," Rogers said. "They’ve both have gone off to the left."

"They are very radical, and they are way too extreme for Michigan," he continued. "I mean, Abdul, he has his own special sauce of crazy."

item.title: Pro wrestling legend Dory Funk Jr dead at 85
item.description: Dory Funk Jr. held the NWA worlds championship for over four years and trained stars like Kurt Angle, Adam Copeland and Lita at his Funking Conservatory.
item.content:encoded:
Dory Funk Jr., a pro wrestling legend who competed across the globe and helped train countless stars, has died, WWE announced on Tuesday. He was 85.

Funk began his pro wrestling pursuits in 1963 after he finished his college football career at West Texas A&M University. He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2009.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON FOX NEWS DIGITAL

"Saddened to announce the passing of Dory Funk, Jr.," WWE chief content officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque wrote in a post on X. "From the Double Cross Ranch to the @WWE Hall of Fame, Dory’s style inspired countless performers in our industry. Whether it was at WrestleMania 2, WCW, ECW, or the dozens of NWA-affiliated promotions, his travels across North America and Asia were a part of the early blueprint that helped build this business into a global phenomena.

"A hard-nosed and fierce competitor, his rugged in-ring style was only eclipsed by the decades he spent training athletes to perform in the squared circle he loved so much. My thoughts and those of the entire @WWE Universe are with his loved ones during this difficult time."

Funk started in his father Dory Funk Sr.’s promotion, Western States Sports, in 1963 and got real-world experience wrestling with the likes of Harley Race and others. It was in 1969 when he became the National Wrestling Alliance (NWA) world champion and held the title for more than four years. He would be seen in the NWA until 1987.

"The National Wrestling Alliance is saddened to note the passing of Hall of Fame former NWA Worlds Heavyweight Champion Dory Funk Jr.," the NWA said in a post on X.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"The National Wrestling Alliance sends its most heartfelt wishes to the family, friends and fans of Dory Funk Jr., a true legend whose contributions to professional wrestling are still felt and celebrated to this day."

Funk appeared in WWE (then the World Wrestling Federation) in 1986, teaming with his brother Terry to start. He had matches there against Junkyard Dog, Tito Santana and Pedro Morales but only remained there for one year.

He wrestled at All Japan Pro Wrestling, Extreme Championship Wrestling and several other promotions before calling it a career in 2017.

WWE inducted Funk into its Hall of Fame as part of its 2009 class. He went in as a tag team with his brother, Terry. The Von Erichs, Bill Watts, Howard Finkel, Koko B. Ware, Ricky Steamboat and "Stone Cold" Steve Austin were also a part of the class.

Funk’s wrestling legacy lives on through the people he trained at his school called The Funking Conservatory. Kurt Angle, Adam Copeland, Christian Cage, Mickie James, Lita and others were among his students.

item.title: Fetterman gives Dems a stinging reality check as Mao-praising communists seize the spotlight
item.description: John Fetterman warns Democrats are drifting toward radical politics as communist sympathizers and anti-Israel voices gain influence after primary results.
item.content:encoded:
Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman railed against the growing influence of socialists and communists in the Democratic Party on Tuesday, warning that figures such as socialist streamer Hasan Piker are pulling the party toward a more radical future.

"I would never try to elevate … a communist just because [Piker] has followers on some, on Twitch, whatever that is. But overall, if you identify with a communist who praises Mao and Cuba and for these places, that should be foreign to any Democrat. Without a doubt, that's having an impact," Fetterman told Fox News Digital on the sidelines of the Israel on Campus Coalition conference Tuesday.

Piker has emerged as an influential voice on the Democratic left, backing socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and campaigning alongside Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed as left-wing candidates court his millions of online followers. Piker has openly praised Mao Zedong and carried water for Cuba’s communist regime, blaming America for the island’s suffering. 

Speaking with Fox News Digital after addressing the Israel on Campus Coalition's National Leadership Summit in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday, Fetterman said the direction of his party has become "troubling" and pointed to Tuesday’s primaries as the latest test of whether Democrats will continue embracing candidates aligned with the party’s progressive flank.

JOHN FETTERMAN MAKES IT 'VERY CLEAR' THAT HE'S 'NOT GOING TO BE A REPUBLICAN' DESPITE DEM BACKLASH

Democratic establishment candidates notched several victories in Tuesday night’s primaries, including Rep. Wesley Bell’s defeat of DSA-backed former Rep. Cori Bush’s comeback bid in Missouri. The high-stakes Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, however, remained too close to call early Wednesday, with Abdul El-Sayed, who has drawn support from prominent socialists, facing the more moderate Rep. Haley Stevens.

"I see the midterms right now that the more radical, the more anti-Israel, and the people have turned Israel as to the ultimate litmus … When you have Gov. Newsom describing Israel as an apartheid state. He knows better, that that's not true," said Fetterman.

The Pennsylvania Democrat continued that it should be "pretty obvious" that the party should not "pander to the fringe." 

"Those are core values. … Like I said, you just can't pander to those kinds of people," he added.

President Donald Trump issued his own warning earlier this summer, arguing that the Democratic Party had moved far beyond socialism.

"These are not social Democrats," Trump said in June following socialists notching primary wins in New York. "These are hardcore, godless communists. They're godless communists. All communists are godless. They don't believe in God. This is the most serious threat to our country since its existence. In my opinion, 250 years ago. This is a major threat to our country."

FETTERMAN CALLS ZOHRAN MAMDANI A 'CLOWN' OVER PUSH TO ARREST NETANYAHU IN NEW YORK CITY

When asked by a reporter late Tuesday night what it would mean if more socialists prevailed in primary races, Trump said the Democratic Party is a "mess."

"I think they should form another party, the communist of America party. I think they should have a new party, the communists of America, and it will do well, it'll get about 10% of the vote," Trump said.

Fetterman spoke at the Israel on Campus Coalition’s flagship event, which brought more than 800 pro-Israel students to Washington for advocacy training, networking and discussions on supporting Israel, combating antisemitism and strengthening the U.S.-Israel relationship on college campuses.

Fetterman said the shift in the Democratic Party is evident in how even pro-Israel Democrats now feel pressure to qualify their support for the Jewish state.

"The left is using the term of Zionist as like a slur or use Zio or Zio, or describing that as someone that in the negative terms," Fetterman said. "In other words, being proud, pro-Israel, that's become a slur, and people have to defend that."

TRUMP WARNS ‘GODLESS COMMUNISTS’ WILL TURN CITIES INTO SLUMS AS DEMS FAIL TO FIGHT SOCIALIST SURGE

Fetterman also pointed to Iran as another defining fault line within the Democratic Party, defending the Trump administration’s strikes on the country’s nuclear facilities and highlighting his break with most Senate Democrats over presidential war powers.

"I think I was the only Democrat to support the Trump administration to bomb the Iranian nuclear facilities," said Fetterman. "If you don't want them to acquire a nuclear bomb, it's pretty reasonable to bomb their nuclear facilities, they want to build one. And overall, the Iranian war, I've remained the only Democrat to vote against the War Power[s] Act."

"I would say that for almost half a century, every American president had been trying to address the problem with Iran. The problem is Iran. That's the problem," he added.

item.title: Grocer-turned-lawmaker says Mamdani’s government-run stores 'might not even last a year’
item.description: Rep. Mike Rulli, a former grocer, warns Zohran Mamdani's government-run grocery stores will bleed red and put hundreds of small businesses out.
item.content:encoded:
A former grocer is joining the chorus of criticism against New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's plan for government-run grocery stores, arguing it would harm hundreds of small businesses forced to compete with them.

"That supermarket will just bleed red the entire time it's open, from the first time you turn the key until it closes," Rep. Mike Rulli, R-Ohio, told Fox News Digital. "And I would bet the farm there's no way these grocery stores last more than five years — they might not even last a year."

Rulli grew up with his family's Ohio-based grocery store chain, Rulli Brothers, which is now run by his brothers.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

Rulli said his family's small but thriving two-location business has given him an appreciation for the challenges facing small business owners in New York City, whom he argued would be harmed by competition from Mamdani's city-run stores.

"You will put hundreds of these small businesses out of business. And a lot of these businesses are owned by immigrants," Rulli said. "So I mean, I don't think the mayor could possibly have asked for a worse situation."

NY GOVERNOR HOPEFUL VOWS SHOWDOWN WITH MAMDANI OVER SOCIALIST AGENDA: ‘I WILL STOP HIM’

Mamdani, the Democratic socialist mayor of New York City, unveiled a plan for government-funded grocery stores while on the campaign trail. The city has since committed $70 million to constructing one store in each of the five boroughs, with an aim to open all five by 2030.

Mamdani discussed the agreement during a recent news conference, saying, "Once a month, our five city-run grocery stores will set prices for this core set of goods at 30% below typical retail prices."

MAMDANI’S CITY GROCERY PLAN COULD LEAVE TAXPAYERS PAYING FOR EVERY BANANA

While the plan has been cheered by progressives, it has been panned by business groups such as the Multicultural Business Coalition, which the New York Post reported was threatening to sue Mamdani.

Rulli, noting that grocery stores already operate on thin profit margins, said Mamdani's government shops will likely be "operating at a loss the entire time."

"When you think about the grocery industry, [it] runs on about 27% gross. That's before you pay your bills. Once you pay your bills, you're about one-and-a-quarter, one-and-half-percent net," he said.

item.title: GOP Rep Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after House ethics report recommends censure
item.description: Republican Rep. Chuck Edwards of North Carolina dropped his re-election bid in the wake of the release of a House Ethics Committee report.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announced early on Wednesday morning that he was dropping his re-election bid.

"After much prayer and reflection, I’ve decided to withdraw from my re-election campaign. I will complete my current term. Serving Western North Carolina has been the honor of my life. Thank you for your trust, prayers, and support. God bless WNC and America," Edwards noted in a post on X that was published at 3:32 a.m. ET.

The announcement came two days after the House Ethics Committee released a report recommending Edwards' censure.

GOP LAWMAKER'S GIFTS, 'EFFUSIVE AFFECTION' TOWARD YOUNG STAFFERS DETAILED IN EXPLOSIVE ETHICS REPORT

Fox News Digital reached out to Edwards' congressional office and campaign on Wednesday morning.

Edwards has served in the U.S. House of Representatives since early 2023.

He decisively won the GOP primary in North Carolina's 11th Congressional District earlier this year.

'MCDONALD'S CHANGED THE COURSE OF MY LIFE': CONGRESSMAN SELLS BUSINESS HE BUILT SINCE HIS TEEN YEARS

But on Monday, the House Committee on Ethics issued a report finding Edwards "engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."

While Edwards "denied that any of his conduct was intended as a sexual or romantic advance, his pattern of behavior would lead a reasonable observer to interpret it as such, including providing the young women with lavish and recurrent gifts, making comments regarding their appearance and dress, inviting them to intimate dinners and vacations, sending notes regarding his effusive affection, and inviting them to other activities as a way to spend time together," the report says.

The committee said it found "no evidence that Representative Edwards engaged in sexual activity with or explicitly propositioned any individual under his employ."

Edwards "was aware, however, that his excessive attention toward the young women had led to rumors and innuendo in the office," the report says. "Both women were uncomfortable with his behavior (which they attempted to communicate) but were put in an untenable position by virtue of his status as their boss and a Member of Congress. Representative Edwards was at minimum blind to that reality, and at worst, dismissive of the impact his inappropriate conduct had on the careers and wellbeing of two women on his staff."

REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER WELCOMES HOUSE ETHICS PROBE INTO SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS AGAINST HIM

"The Committee hereby adopts this Report in this matter and recommends Representative Edwards be censured for his conduct," the document noted.
